utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Madam Registrar. We are here today for a Pre-Trial Conference in the case of Mr. Gotovina, Mr Cermak, and Mr. Markac. I would like to have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Alan Tieger, Stefan Waespi, Katarina Gustafson, and case manager Donnica Henry Frijlink for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Then for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Gregory Kehoe, Luka Misetic, Payam Akhavan and Ana Katalinic for General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Then for Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On behalf of Mr. Cermak, Steven Kay, Andrew Cayley, and Tihomir Mak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Kay, and then finally Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: For General Markac, Goran Mikulicic, Tomislav Kuzmanovic, and Vlado Rendulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd first like to inform the parties that this morning Judge Kinis was sworn in as a Judge. That means that the decision on the composition of this Bench for this case has now become effective on from this morning, and therefore I'm glad to introduce to you Judge Gwaunza to my left, Judge Kinis to my right, and not a surprise, I'm Judge Orie for those who would not know yet. I think we have a relatively short agenda for this Pre-Trial Conference. At a 65 ter Conference last week, a lot of matters were raised. I also do understand that the parties have sat together and have resolved a number of the issues. There are other issues which are not ready yet to be determined. I think the first thing I have to do is to give you a decision on the Prosecution's motion to amend its witness list, a motion that was filed on the 1st of February of this year. So I'll now proceed to deliver that decision. It's a decision on the Prosecution's motion to amend its witness list filed on the 1st of February, 2008. On the 18th of February, 2008, the Gotovina Defence filed a response requesting the Trial Chamber to deny the Prosecution leave withdraw Steinar Hjertnes from the Prosecution's witness list and deny the Prosecution leave to add Tor Munkelein in his place. The response further requested that the Trial Chamber deny the Prosecution to leave to convert all of its witnesses into potential 92 ter witnesses. On the 25th of February, 2008, the Prosecution filed a request for leave to reply and a reply to the Gotovina Defence's response, and the Trial Chamber granted leave to reply on the 28th of February and informally communicated this to the parties. The Trial Chamber grants the Prosecution's motion to amend its witness list and adopts the number of witnesses the Prosecutor wishes to call, and adopts the time available to the Prosecutor for presenting evidence. The reasons for this decision will follow in writing at a later stage. And this concludes the decision on the Prosecution's motion to amend its witness list. Where the decision refers to the number of witnesses and the time available for presenting evidence, I remind you that on the new list the Prosecution asked for 209.5 hours to present 134 witnesses, out of which it is proposed by the Prosecution that 112 will be in court to testify viva voce or partly, most of them partly, under Rule 92 ter. Of course decisions on the remaining 22 witnesses, whether the Chamber allows these witnesses to testify under Rule 92 bis, still are to be taken, and the same is true for the admission of witness statements under Rule 92 quater, 92 quater dealing with witnesses that have deceased or are not available. It was announced last Thursday that the first witness would not take two hours but only half an hour. The Chamber nevertheless thought it wise not to immediately reduce the 209.5 hours to 208 hours. So therefore, Mr. Tieger, it's still 209.5 hours. As I said before, the reasons for this decision going in further detail as far as the objections made by the parties are concerned will follow in writing. Next item on my agenda is the exhibit list. The Chamber, although I have not seen it yet but received a courtesy copy of a new proposed exhibit list. I don't know whether its yet filed or not, Mr. Tieger, but you'll understand that in the very short time we had available, not having considered any responses by the Defence and also not having dealt with translation issues, for example, that it's impossible for at this moment to deliver any decision on that. At the same time we'll hear from the Defence soon, and we'll try to resolve this matter as quickly as possible. From what I understand, there's no specific issue any more about Witness 136, who is the first witness to testify this week. I do understand that as far as the exhibits are concerned that an agreement was reached where the party requested -- where the bench requested the parties to sit together that finally an agreement was reached on the exhibits to be introduced through Witness 136. Is there any matter related to one of the issues I raised that needs attention at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I must have missed that colloquy on the exhibits for 136. I certainly know Mr. Misetic was part of that discussion. I will gladly have that discussion with the Prosecution before 136 takes the stand. I believe it's not until Thursday, but I was not part of that discussion, nor did I know it was taking place. Maybe I missed something during the 65 ter Conference. If that's the case I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kehoe, did you take any steps to get together with Mr. Tieger on exhibits issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the exhibit issues go on daily. I mean I got another swath of exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No I mean last Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour I travelled on Friday to come here, and I have not with all due respect. But with regard to exhibits from the Defence side, and I speak just for General Gotovina, but I do believe that my colleagues will echo this, that the exhibits that are continually being given to us and information given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but it was a specific invitation during the 65 ter Conference to try to resolve matters of portions of exhibits to be tendered instead of the whole so that it would not be necessary for the Chamber to rule on partial inadmissibility. There was a clear invitation for that, and it was also clear, I think, as a matter of fact, because it was dealt with in relation with, I think, especially also the exhibits, I remember the lists, et cetera, in relation to the first witness. So therefore it surprises me a bit that you were not even aware. That means not great communication between Defence counsel on this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect as you know I had a family obligation back in the United States. That's why I wasn't here. I had an event with my daughter to take care of. However, Your Honour, I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's be fair --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will in fact -- I will in fact go through the exhibits and talk to Mr. Tieger -- or Mr. Waespi specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But I stand up and I bring it to Your Honour's attention because I didn't want to be incorporated into that until I have a chance to go through this and talk to Mr. Waespi, which I'll gladly do this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think furthermore there was an issue of further argument on these kind of matters today if no resolution was achieved, but let's be very practical. I take it that you will ask your colleagues about the reasons or what made them agree with the Prosecution and then you get together with Mr. Tieger, Mr. Waespi and see whether you can join the agreement reached. If not, then of course we'll have to decide on the exhibits either before the witness appears or when the witness is in court and when these exhibits are tendered. Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's just one matter of clarification on Witness 136. We have had our meeting with the Prosecution. Agreement has been reached between the parties save for one matter, and we're reflecting upon this severally and jointly today, but it's a matter that I believe may well be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When I printed out yesterday evening the list of exhibits on which there was agreement, I saw that one of them was still in red rather than in black. I don't know whether that's the issue. Of course I wondered what it meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will be dealing with the matter. It just needs a review and a thinking by both sides of their respective positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Mr. Kehoe can already join in that exercise. If there's any remaining issue there, the Chamber would like to be informed in the usual way, that is, first of all through an e-mail message to the legal officer in charge of this case, which is Mr. Nilsson normally. I don't see him here at this moment. Is there any other matter, because if we're talking about -- there's of course one other remaining issue in relation to Witness 136 but not to be dealt with at this moment. Perhaps I could ask, first of all, to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Then the Chamber has received, as I'm informed because I've not read it yet, an application for further provisional release for Mr. Cermak. We'll read it. I do understand that the request is to grant further provisional release from the end of this week until the 7th of April, or at least a couple of days before that. We'll consider the matter. Just for you to be aware that the Chamber is aware of this motion pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There is a supplemental to that motion that has been filed ex parte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll look at that as well. Then just to remind the parties the -- tomorrow, the 11th of March at 9.00 in the morning, the Chamber will start hearing the Prosecution's opening statement. Then on Wednesday, the 12th of March, 9.00 in the morning, the Chamber will hear the Gotovina Defence opening statement. The other two accused, Mr. Cermak and Mr. Markac, have refrained from an opening statement, at least at this moment. Whether they'll make an opening statement or not is still to be seen, but if so, it will be a delayed opening statement. And then on the 13th of March we'll hear the first evidence to be presented by the Prosecution. These were all the matters I have on my agenda. Is there anything one of the parties would like to raise, or is there anything the accused think they should raise at this moment, whether or not closed or in open session, for example, in respect of health issues, detention issues? Perhaps I first ask you, Mr. Tieger. Anything to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. Tom Kuzmanovic here. I do have a question on the issue of something we received via e-mail from Mr. Tieger today, and I guess thought I'd bring it up in open court right now. We received about a 15 or 16-page index of documentation that the OTP is apparently in the process of receiving, most of which relates to our client, and the question I have is is this going to be added to the exhibit list that we already have? Is the exhibit list going to be modified? When is there anything to be a decision on whether or not any of this material is going to be used? We haven't seen it either yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, I understand from Mr. Kuzmanovic that you're in the process of receiving materials and that you are sending lists or indexes of that material. Could you -- is this material that has come to your attention recently, or is it -- could you further clarify the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. The answer is very recently. Actually, on Friday, and the material has not even yet physically arrived here in The Hague. I advised Mr. Kuzmanovic and Mr. Mikulicic that we would process that as quickly as possible. I wanted them to know immediately that we had received the material and it would be arriving and to indicate to them what it was we provided them with an index of that material. That's the extent to the information we have about it as well, and we will proceed accordingly. We've asked that it be couriered here so that we receive it as quickly as possible and can process it expeditiously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that it goes without saying that if you have not even physically received or let alone read this material that the issue of whether or not this should be added to the exhibit list is premature to deal with at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kuzmanovic, that is perhaps not a very satisfactory answer, and of course later we'll -- questions will come up as why is it that it only received -- it's received now, what kind of material it is, but I'm afraid at this moment we have to grant some time to Mr. Tieger to at least look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understandably, Your Honour, and I guess my question -- I just wanted to raise it. Let Your Honour know about it in advance. Mr. Tieger did advise us of this material. He did send us an index. There is -- you know, that was all done very properly and we appreciate it, and I just wanted to know if there was any indication at all in the near future as to when we would find out about it in more detail. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The only thing I'd add, Your Honour, is that the index indicates that it's potentially documentation of considerable relevance related to the accused and to close associates of the accused. So it does need to be reviewed quickly and carefully, but certainly the potential for a motion to add to the exhibit list is high.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I do understand, but this all at this moment speculative, and as it is also speculative on whether at this late stage good cause to be shown at all whether now new material should be added to the exhibit list, yes or no. We'll just give you some time, Mr. Tieger, since you -- and the Chamber urges you since it is very new material to do it as quickly as possible. Any other matter, Mr. Kuzmanovic or Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I address you, Mr. Gotovina, Mr. Cermak, and Mr. Markac. Is there anything you'd like to raise? And of course I expect you to deal with the most -- the legal and the technical matters through counsel, but if there's any personal matter you'd like to raise, please do so. Mr. Gotovina. THE ACCUSED GOTOVINA: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you for your attention. I have no questions. I am ready to go, and I leave the rest to my Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Cermak. THE ACCUSED CERMAK: [Interpretation] Nothing to raise, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Markac. THE ACCUSED MARKAC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there's nothing on the agenda any more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there's nothing on my agenda anymore and since my colleagues have no matters to be raised at this moment, this concludes the Pre-Trial Conference. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning; that is the 11th of March. In this same courtroom, Madam Registrar. Same courtroom, Courtroom III. We stand adjourned.
